paragraphs: Before the shift, receive drawings and blanks. In the morning, turn and mill parts and measure dimensions with calipers. After midday, use 3D printing for supplemental pieces and file seams and apply putty. In the afternoon, conduct trial assembly, inspect fit, sand, and paint. Before leaving, deliver the prototype, record the work order, and clean the workstation.
In short, they turn drawings into tangible prototypes. They turn, mill, print, fit, measure, and test assemblies, working with both machines and files as the physical-production side of R&D.
